coverTitle:
Five Prayers
For What You
Lost and Still Carry
coverDek: For the empty chair, the phone number you haven't deleted, the version of life that didn't happen — five prayers for grief that hasn't finished with you yet.

points.hook: Lord, everyone else has moved on. I haven't.
paragraphs: The calls stopped coming a long time ago. The casseroles stopped. Everybody went back to their ordinary Tuesdays, and I'm still standing in the spot where my life changed, wondering why it still hurts like it's new. I've started to feel ashamed of how long this is taking.

But You never put a calendar on mourning. You wept at a grave You were about to empty — not because You didn't have power, but because loss is still loss, even on its way to being undone. Sit with me in what hasn't healed yet. I'm not behind schedule. I'm just still loving someone I lost.

points.hook: I decree it today: sorrow is not the last word over my life.
paragraphs: I speak to every grief that has tried to convince me joy is finished — I reject that lie in the name of Jesus! Weeping endures for a night, but joy comes in the morning. I am not denying the night. I am declaring that it is not forever.
I call my mourning what God calls it: a season, not a sentence. I decree that beauty will come for these ashes, and the spirit of heaviness will not have the last say over me, in Jesus' mighty name!
points.verseText: Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.

points.hook: Notice what grief is doing to your body right now.
paragraphs: It's the exhaustion that sleep doesn't fix. The appetite that disappeared or won't stop. The chest that feels tight for no reason you can point to today. Grief isn't only in your mind — it moves through your whole body, and pretending otherwise just makes you carry it alone.

God doesn't ask you to grieve efficiently. He promises to be near the brokenhearted — near, not distant, not disappointed in how long it's taking your body to catch up to what your heart already knows. Let your shoulders drop. Let the tears come if they're there. That's not weakness. That's your body finally being honest.
points.verseText: The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.

points.hook: Somebody reading this is grieving alone because nobody knows how to sit with it.
paragraphs: Job's friends got it right for seven days — they sat with him in the ashes and said nothing, because some grief doesn't need an answer, it needs a presence. It was only when they opened their mouths to explain it that they made it worse.

Family, if you're carrying this by yourself, say so out loud to someone. And if someone you love is grieving, you don't need the right words today — you need to show up and stay. We were never meant to grieve in a room by ourselves.
points.verseText: So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great.

points.hook: Child, I know exactly which tear is which.
paragraphs: You've cried some of these tears where no one could see you — in the car, in the shower, in the three a.m. quiet where the loss is loudest. I was there for every one. Not a single one fell where I wasn't watching.

One day I will wipe every one of them away myself, and death, the thing that started all of this, won't even be a memory worth mentioning. Until that day, rest here. I'm not in a hurry with your healing, and I'm not going anywhere while you grieve.
points.verseText: And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.

cta.closingLine: If even one of these named what you're carrying, don't carry it alone today — come back tomorrow for the next series.
